t: This is Levita House and The Somers Town Coffee House, a pairing of 1930s public housing and a public house in Somers Town. The architect was G. Topham Forrest, who lived from 1872 to 1945. He was a Scottish architect who became chief architect for the London County Council. In that role he designed many public housing estates, and he also co-designed two bridges over the River Thames. So what's in front of you is a piece of the council's housing programme of the period, drawn by the man who led its architects.
